title: "dcb_oxalate_combined"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## Overview

Teneille's full project repository is available at <https://github.com/Teneille97/rocmics>.

We analysed metal(loid)s (Fe, Al, Mn and Si) extracted by DCB and oxalate in soils from an enhanced rock weathering field trial in Malle. The DCB extraction is designed for reductive dissolution of more crystalline Fe oxides and the oxalate extraction is designed for ligand-assisted dissolution of poorly crystalline/amorphous/short-range-order phases.

## DCB- and oxalate-extractable metal(loid) content of different treatments

We observe more oxalate-extractable metals released from Bolsdorfer treatment, especially Si. In the dose-response experiment, Huhnerberg dose response clearly shows oxalate-extractable Al & Mn decrease, probably associating with more crystalline oxides.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: metal(loid)s comparison
#| warning: FALSE
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
#| out-width: 100%

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LIBRARIES & SETUP
# ==============================================================================
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(emmeans)
library(multcomp)
library(multcompView)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# Set global ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_bw())

# ==============================================================================
# 2. METADATA PROCESSING
# ==============================================================================
metadata <- read.csv(here("csv_files", "treatment_names.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_group = case_when(
      Treatment == "Control" ~ "Control",
      Treatment == "Eifelgold_50" ~ "Eifelgold_50",
      Treatment == "Bolsdorfer_50" ~ "Bolsdorfer_50",
      Treatment == "Lime_2" ~ "Lime_2",
      Treatment == "Huhnerberg_50" ~ "Huhnerberg_50",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. IMPORT & CLEAN OXALATE DATA (mg g^-1)
# ==============================================================================
oxalate_raw <- read.csv(here("csv_files", "oxalate_sesq_feb2026.csv"))

oxalate_long <- cbind(oxalate_raw, metadata) %>%
  separate(Treatment, into = c("Tmt", "App_rate"), sep = "_", fill = "right") %>%
  mutate(
    App_rate = replace_na(App_rate, "0"),
    Tmt = factor(Tmt),
    App_rate = factor(App_rate, levels = c("0", "2", "4", "8", "12", "20", "30", "50")),
    Method = "Oxalate"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, analysis_group, Tmt, App_rate, Method,
                Fe = Fe..mg.g.1.soil.,
                Al = Al..mg.g.1.soil.,
                Mn = Mn..mg.g.1.soil.,
                Si = Si..mg.g.1.soil.) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Fe, Al, Mn, Si),
    names_to = "Element",
    values_to = "Concentration"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 4. IMPORT & CLEAN DCB DATA (Converted to mg g^-1: % * 10)
# ==============================================================================
dcb_raw <- read.csv(here("csv_files", "DCB_Feb2026.csv"))

# Note: Converting elemental % to mg g^-1 by multiplying by 10 (1% = 10 mg/g)
dcb_long <- cbind(dcb_raw, metadata) %>%
  separate(Treatment, into = c("Tmt", "App_rate"), sep = "_", fill = "right") %>%
  mutate(
    App_rate = replace_na(App_rate, "0"),
    Tmt = factor(Tmt),
    App_rate = factor(App_rate, levels = c("0", "2", "4", "8", "12", "20", "30", "50")),
    Method = "DCB",
    # Column conversions if elemental % columns exist
    Fe = if("X.Fe" %in% names(.)) X.Fe * 10 else NA_real_,
    Al = X.Al * 10,
    Mn = X.Mn * 10,
    Si = X.Si * 10
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, analysis_group, Tmt, App_rate, Method, Fe, Al, Mn, Si) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Fe, Al, Mn, Si),
    names_to = "Element",
    values_to = "Concentration"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 5. UNIFIED DATASET & METRIC CALCULATIONS (DIFFERENCES & RATIOS)
# ==============================================================================
# Combined long dataset for extractions
combined_extractions <- bind_rows(oxalate_long, dcb_long)

# Reshape wide to compute sample-matched ratios and differences
extraction_metrics <- combined_extractions %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Method,
    values_from = Concentration
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Diff_DCB_Ox = DCB - Oxalate,           # Crystalline/Residual fraction (e.g., Fe_d - Fe_o)
    Ratio_Ox_DCB = Oxalate / DCB           # Amorphous/Active fraction ratio (e.g., Fe_o / Fe_d)
  )

# Convert metrics to long format for easy visualization
metrics_long <- extraction_metrics %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Diff_DCB_Ox, Ratio_Ox_DCB),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 6. COMBINED PLOTS: OXALATE VS DCB (SHARED SCALE)
# ==============================================================================

# Custom Color Palette
method_colors <- c("Oxalate" = "#E69F00", "DCB" = "#56B4E9")

# --- 50 t/ha Treatments Comparison (ANOVA & Tukey Letters) ---
plot50_combined <- combined_extractions %>%
  filter(analysis_group %in% c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")) %>%
  mutate(analysis_group = factor(analysis_group, levels = c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")))

# Generate Tukey Letters per Element and Extraction Method
letters_df_combined <- plot50_combined %>%
  group_by(Element, Method) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    mod <- aov(Concentration ~ analysis_group, data = .x)
    emm <- emmeans(mod, ~ analysis_group)
    cld_res <- cld(emm, Letters = letters, adjust = "tukey")
    
    cld_res %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::select(analysis_group, .group) %>%
      mutate(
        .group = str_trim(.group),
        y = max(.x$Concentration, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.08
      )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(plot50_combined, aes(x = analysis_group, y = Concentration, fill = Method)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.7,
    position = position_dodge(0.8)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = Method),
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.1,
      dodge.width = 0.8
    ),
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_df_combined,
    aes(
      x = analysis_group,
      y = y,
      label = .group,
      group = Method
    ),
    position = position_dodge(0.8),
    size = 3.5,
    vjust = 0
  ) +
  facet_grid(Element ~ Method, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.20))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = expression(paste("Concentration (mg g"^-1, " soil)")),
    title = "50 t/ha Group Comparisons with Post-Hoc Tukey Groups"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Dose-Response (Huhnerberg vs Control) ---
dose_resp_combined <- combined_extractions %>%
  filter(Tmt == "Control" | Tmt == "Huhnerberg") %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = ifelse(Tmt == "Control", "Control", paste0(App_rate, " t ha^-1")),
    Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "2 t ha^-1", "4 t ha^-1", "8 t ha^-1", "12 t ha^-1", "20 t ha^-1", "30 t ha^-1", "50 t ha^-1"))
  )

ggplot(dose_resp_combined, aes(x = Treatment, y = Concentration, fill = Method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Method), position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8), size = 1.8) +
  facet_grid(Element ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = expression(paste("Concentration (mg g"^-1, " soil)")),
    title = "Dose-Response Comparison (Huhnerberg)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

## Ratio comparison

We then compared the ratio of oxalate- to DCB-extractable elements among treatments.

We see much higher oxalate-Si relative to DCB-Si in the Bolsdorfer treatment, consistent with the presence of poorly crystalline Si-bearing phases. Meanwhile, iron-bearing minerals in the basalts release Fe2+ upon weathering, which can oxidize and form crystalline iron oxides. More DCB-Fe relative to oxalate-Fe in the treatments compared to control is consistent with the development or aging of Fe oxide phases following Fe release and oxidation during basalt weathering.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: ratio comparison
#| warning: FALSE
#| 
metrics_50 <- extraction_metrics %>%
  filter(analysis_group %in% c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")) %>%
  mutate(analysis_group = factor(analysis_group, levels = c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")))


# 1. Filter metrics data for the 50 t/ha comparison group
ratio_50 <- extraction_metrics %>%
  filter(analysis_group %in% c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")) %>%
  mutate(analysis_group = factor(analysis_group, levels = c("Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50", "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2")))

# 2. Calculate Tukey HSD compact letter displays (CLD) per Element for Ratio_Ox_DCB
letters_ratio_df <- ratio_50 %>%
  group_by(Element) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    # Run ANOVA model on Ratio_Ox_DCB
    mod <- aov(Ratio_Ox_DCB ~ analysis_group, data = .x)
    
    # Estimate marginal means
    emm <- emmeans(mod, ~ analysis_group)
    
    # Compute Tukey pairwise comparisons and letter groups
    cld_results <- cld(
      emm,
      Letters = letters,
      adjust = "tukey"
    )
    
    # Format letters and calculate label y-position slightly above max ratio value
    cld_results %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::select(analysis_group, .group) %>%
      mutate(
        .group = str_trim(.group),
        y = max(.x$Ratio_Ox_DCB, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.10
      )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Plot Amorphous Fraction Ratio with Tukey Letters
ggplot(ratio_50, aes(x = analysis_group, y = Ratio_Ox_DCB)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "grey92",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    color = "#2B5C8F"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_ratio_df,
    aes(
      x = analysis_group,
      y = y,
      label = .group
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  facet_grid(Element ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = expression(paste("Active Ratio (Oxalate / DCB)")),
    title = "Amorphous Fraction Ratio (Oxalate / DCB) with Tukey HSD Groups"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
  )
# ==============================================================================
# Dose-response ratio plot (Hühnerberg)
# No statistical comparisons because there are no replicates
# ==============================================================================

dose_resp_ratio <- extraction_metrics %>%
  filter(Tmt == "Control" | Tmt == "Huhnerberg") %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = ifelse(
      Tmt == "Control",
      "Control",
      paste0(App_rate, " t ha^-1")
    ),
    Treatment = factor(
      Treatment,
      levels = c(
        "Control",
        "2 t ha^-1",
        "4 t ha^-1",
        "8 t ha^-1",
        "12 t ha^-1",
        "20 t ha^-1",
        "30 t ha^-1",
        "50 t ha^-1"
      )
    )
  )


ggplot(
  dose_resp_ratio,
  aes(x = Treatment, y = Ratio_Ox_DCB, group = 1)
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    Element ~ .,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = expression(paste("Active Ratio (Oxalate / DCB)")),
    title = "Dose-Response Comparison (Hühnerberg)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 10
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 13
    )
  )
```

## Secondary-mineral geochemical ratios by treatment

Elemental ratios (Al:Si, Fe:Si and Al:Fe) were calculated separately for oxalate- and DCB-extractable concentrations for each soil plot. These ratios are operational geochemical indicators and should not be interpreted as definitive mineral identifications. Treatment comparisons are shown for the Control, Bolsdorfer (50 t ha⁻¹), Eifelgold (50 t ha⁻¹), Hühnerberg (50 t ha⁻¹), and Lime (2 t ha⁻¹) groups.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: secondary mineral ratios by treatment
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 14
#| out-width: 100%

# ==============================================================================
# 9. SECONDARY-MINERAL GEOCHEMICAL RATIOS
# ==============================================================================
# Calculates element ratios separately for oxalate and DCB extractions.
# Each row represents an individual soil sample/plot.
#
# Ratios are operational geochemical indicators, not definitive mineral IDs.
# All elemental concentrations must be expressed in the same units.
# ==============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(multcomp)
library(multcompView)

# ==============================================================================
# 9. SECONDARY-MINERAL GEOCHEMICAL RATIOS
# ==============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(multcomp)
library(multcompView)

treatment_levels <- c(
  "Control", "Bolsdorfer_50", "Eifelgold_50",
  "Huhnerberg_50", "Lime_2"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.1 Calculate ratios separately for each extraction method and plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ratio_wide <- combined_extractions %>%
  dplyr::select(
    sample, analysis_group, Tmt, App_rate, Method,
    Element, Concentration
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Element,
    values_from = Concentration
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Oxalate-extractable ratios
    Ox_Al_Si = if_else(Si > 0, Al / Si, NA_real_),
    Ox_Fe_Si = if_else(Si > 0, Fe / Si, NA_real_),
    Ox_Al_Fe = if_else(Fe > 0, Al / Fe, NA_real_),
    
    # DCB-extractable ratios
    DCB_Al_Si = if_else(Si > 0, Al / Si, NA_real_),
    DCB_Fe_Si = if_else(Si > 0, Fe / Si, NA_real_),
    DCB_Al_Fe = if_else(Fe > 0, Al / Fe, NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        Ox_Al_Si, Ox_Fe_Si, Ox_Al_Fe,
        DCB_Al_Si, DCB_Fe_Si, DCB_Al_Fe
      ),
      ~ if_else(is.finite(.x), .x, NA_real_)
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9.2 Long-format dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ratio_long <- ratio_wide %>%
  dplyr::select(
    sample, analysis_group, Tmt, App_rate, Method,
    Ox_Al_Si, Ox_Fe_Si, Ox_Al_Fe,
    DCB_Al_Si, DCB_Fe_Si, DCB_Al_Fe
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      Ox_Al_Si, Ox_Fe_Si, Ox_Al_Fe,
      DCB_Al_Si, DCB_Fe_Si, DCB_Al_Fe
    ),
    names_to = "Ratio",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    (Method == "Oxalate" & str_starts(Ratio, "Ox_")) |
      (Method == "DCB" & str_starts(Ratio, "DCB_"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Ratio = recode(
      Ratio,
      Ox_Al_Si = "Oxalate Al:Si",
      Ox_Fe_Si = "Oxalate Fe:Si",
      Ox_Al_Fe = "Oxalate Al:Fe",
      DCB_Al_Si = "DCB Al:Si",
      DCB_Fe_Si = "DCB Fe:Si",
      DCB_Al_Fe = "DCB Al:Fe"
    )
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 10. TUKEY HSD TREATMENT COMPARISONS
# ==============================================================================

ratio_50 <- ratio_long %>%
  filter(analysis_group %in% treatment_levels) %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_group = factor(
      analysis_group,
      levels = treatment_levels
    )
  )

# ANOVA results for each ratio
ratio_anova_results <- ratio_50 %>%
  group_by(Ratio) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    
    dat <- .x %>%
      filter(is.finite(Value)) %>%
      droplevels()
    
    if (n_distinct(dat$analysis_group) < 2 ||
        nrow(dat) <= n_distinct(dat$analysis_group)) {
      return(tibble(
        n = nrow(dat),
        F_statistic = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_
      ))
    }
    
    fit <- aov(Value ~ analysis_group, data = dat)
    tab <- summary(fit)[[1]]
    
    tibble(
      n = nrow(dat),
      F_statistic = unname(tab[1, "F value"]),
      p_value = unname(tab[1, "Pr(>F)"])
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_adjusted_BH = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.1 Tukey HSD compact letter displays
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ratio_tukey_results <- ratio_50 %>%
  group_by(Ratio) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    
    dat <- .x %>%
      filter(is.finite(Value)) %>%
      droplevels()
    
    if (n_distinct(dat$analysis_group) < 2 ||
        nrow(dat) <= n_distinct(dat$analysis_group)) {
      return(tibble(
        analysis_group = character(),
        mean = numeric(),
        SE = numeric(),
        .group = character()
      ))
    }
    
    fit <- aov(Value ~ analysis_group, data = dat)
    emm <- emmeans(fit, ~ analysis_group)
    
    cld(emm, Letters = letters, adjust = "tukey") %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      transmute(
        analysis_group = as.character(analysis_group),
        mean = emmean,
        SE = SE,
        .group = str_trim(.group)
      )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10.2 Plot: treatment ratios WITH Tukey HSD letters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate an appropriate label height for each ratio.
ratio_label_positions <- ratio_50 %>%
  group_by(Ratio) %>%
  summarise(
    y_min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    y_range = y_max - y_min,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_range = if_else(
      is.finite(y_range) & y_range > 0,
      y_range,
      pmax(abs(y_max), 0.1) * 0.1
    ),
    label_y = y_max + 0.12 * y_range
  )

ratio_letters_plot <- ratio_tukey_results %>%
  left_join(ratio_label_positions, by = "Ratio") %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_group = factor(
      analysis_group,
      levels = treatment_levels
    )
  )

p_ratios_tukey <- ggplot(
  ratio_50,
  aes(x = analysis_group, y = Value)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "grey90",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "#2B5C8F"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = ratio_letters_plot,
    aes(
      x = analysis_group,
      y = label_y,
      label = .group
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Ratio,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.22))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Element concentration ratio (mass basis)",
    title = "Secondary-mineral geochemical ratios by treatment",
    subtitle = "Different Tukey letters indicate significant pairwise differences (p < 0.05)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )


# ==============================================================================
# 11. HÜHNERBERG DOSE-RESPONSE RATIOS
# ==============================================================================

# Dose-response plot only: no Tukey letters are calculated for this plot.

dose_levels <- c("0", "2", "4", "8", "12", "20", "30", "50")

ratio_dose <- ratio_long %>%
  filter(Tmt %in% c("Control", "Huhnerberg")) %>%
  mutate(
    Dose = if_else(
      Tmt == "Control",
      "0",
      as.character(App_rate)
    ),
    Dose = factor(Dose, levels = dose_levels)
  )

p_ratios_dose <- ggplot(
  ratio_dose,
  aes(x = Dose, y = Value)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = "grey90",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "#2B5C8F"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Ratio,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    x = expression("Hühnerberg application rate (t ha"^{-1}*")"),
    y = "Element concentration ratio (mass basis)",
    title = "Hühnerberg dose-response in secondary-mineral ratios",
    subtitle = "Control shown at 0 t ha⁻¹"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_ratios_tukey)
print(p_ratios_dose)


```
